traits.fruit_shape.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: fruit dry, obconical to ellipsoidal (the first named here), tan at maturity.

traits.tubercle_relief.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: tubercles prominent.

traits.spine_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: spines yellow to tan to deep reddish brown, greying; tan here.

traits.spine_colour_aged.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: the spines grey with age.

traits.areole_wool_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: wool white, yellow or tan, ageing greyish black; pale tan here.

traits.flower_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) pp. 204 to 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: flowers bright yellow to bronze to brick red (bronze here, the middle of the words); fruit dry, tan at maturity. Anderson gives the flower's length (2 to 3 cm) but not its width and no fruit size, so their sizes stay set by hand.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) pp. 204 to 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: flowers bright yellow to bronze to brick red (bronze here, the middle of the words); fruit dry, tan at maturity. Anderson gives the flower's length (2 to 3 cm) but not its width and no fruit size, so their sizes stay set by hand.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.64 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.64, branches 0.58. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.lower_areole_spines.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 205, Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: spines 6 to 20, up to 30, mostly on the distal areoles.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, p. 57), as Opuntia acanthocarpa: 8 to 25 needle-like, dark brown spines 2 to 3 cm long (the count's scan is unsure), not told apart as radials and centrals, so stated as radials; glochids numerous, yellow. Their terminal joints, 4 to 8 cm, are shorter than other accounts give, so the joints' length is not stated.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an open, branching shrub 1 to 2 m tall from a short trunk, its slender joints 15 to 50 cm long rising at narrow angles like antlers. Flowers at the joint tips in spring, yellow, orange, red or bronze. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: a metre or more within 15 years. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: grey-green joints with long, raised tubercles, tan sheathed spines in spreading clusters, greying with age. Its flower, bud and fruit are drawn from its characters by the rules at Cactaceae and the flowering plants: tepals on a spiral, as many and as broad as the family's rules give, on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, its stamens, style and stigma lobes, and its fruit from its stated colour, size and surface. Until 2026-10-18 its flower and fruit looks were partly set by hand (round tepal tips, a centre and an accent colour by eye), and a look set by hand keeps the rule that gives it the year its months state from running, so it flowered and fruited all year.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.glochid.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, pp. 42 and 57 to 67): the areoles bear glochids above the spines, here numerous, yellow. Their count, length and angle are set by eye like a prickly pear's, smaller, as no flora measures them.

traits.flowering_months.note: USA-NPN Nature's Notebook phenometrics (getSummarizedData, fetched 2026-10-18; the phenology method of 2026-10-14: each individual-year span of the phenophase counted day by day, keeping the months with at least a third of the busiest month's days), Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa (species 945): 179 open-flower spans on 8 sites, April (393 days) and May (219). The Flora of North America (vol. 4, read on eFloras 2026-10-18) gives spring: May in var. acanthocarpa, March to June in vars. coloradensis and major.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA-NPN Nature's Notebook phenometrics (getSummarizedData, fetched 2026-10-18; the phenology method of 2026-10-14: each individual-year span of the phenophase counted day by day, keeping the months with at least a third of the busiest month's days), Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa (species 945): 905 ripe-fruit spans on 9 sites, most in June to August and above a third of June's days from April to October: the fruit dries tan on the plant (Flora of North America) and stays.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: fruit tan at maturity, obconic to ellipsoid, 15 to 35 by 15 to 20 mm, dry, tuberculate.

traits.anther_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: filaments red; anthers yellow.

traits.filament_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: filaments red; a dark red by hand.

traits.stigma_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: style and stigma lobes white to light green.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa: inner tepals spatulate, 20 to 30 mm; the open flower taken as twice its inner tepals across, by hand, as no flora gives its width (Anderson p. 205: flowers 2 to 3 cm long).
